transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’ve started doing things that honestly kind of scare me. Um, like walking out of work in the middle of system deployments, or just driving around late at night with absolutely no plan. That is really not how I’ve ever handled stress before, so I figured I needed to see someone to figure out what's going on.
Have you been feeling anxious lately?

Yeah, I would say so. It's... well, even on quiet days, I just feel this constant mix of fear and shame sitting right in my chest. Um, it's like I should have handled everything better, and I just have this feeling that something bad could still happen if I let my guard down.
Are you avoiding certain situations or activities because of these feelings of fear and shame?

Yeah, I definitely am. Um, at work, I actually take the long way around the building now. I just avoid that floor whenever I can. And if anyone brings it up... I shut down conversations the moment people start talking about the contractor or the cutover. I just don't want to be near any of it.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body watching yourself do these things that scare you?
No, I don't think I've ever felt like that. I mean, I'm definitely the one doing those things, even if it feels out of character. I'm always completely aware that it's me.
Do you find yourself being extremely perfectionistic or preoccupied with details, to the point where it interferes with your daily life?
No, not really. I mean, I try to do my job well, of course, but I don't think I get overly caught up in tiny details or anything like that. It doesn't get in the way of getting things done.
Do you find yourself having thoughts or memories about the things that scare you that you can't seem to get out of your head?

Yeah, I do. It happens out of nowhere sometimes. Like, especially if I'm near that conference area, or... or even if someone just raises their voice on a call. I'll suddenly get hit with these images and sounds from that night. It comes on so strongly that I completely lose track of what I was saying or doing.
How long have you been experiencing these feelings and reactions?
It's been... well, it started after that late-night cutover incident. So, it's been going on for a little over a year now. Probably about 13 months.
Do you feel numb or detached from yourself or the world around you when those memories or images from that night come back to you?

No, I don't think so. I don't really feel numb or detached when it happens. It's more like... I'm just right back in that moment, feeling all the panic and fear all over again. But I don't feel disconnected from myself or anything.
Are there any specific people, places, or activities that you avoid because they remind you of the cutover incident?

Yeah, definitely. I actually... I take the long way around the building now just to stay away from it. I avoid going up to that floor whenever I possibly can. And it's not just the physical places, either. The moment people start talking about the contractor, or the cutover itself, I just shut the conversation down right away. I really don't want to talk or hear about it.
Do you ever feel like you're reliving the cutover incident, like it's happening all over again, not just remembering it?

Yeah, I do. It happens out of nowhere, really. Like... especially if I have to be anywhere near that conference area, or even if someone just raises their voice on a call. I’ll get hit with the images and the sounds from that night so strongly that I completely lose track of what I was saying. It definitely feels like more than just a memory when it hits me like that.
Has your behavior or these feelings of fear and shame significantly impacted your relationships with friends, family, or your overall work performance?

Yeah, it has. At work, I just had my performance review, and... well, it was the first time I've ever been told I'm missing key handoffs. They said I'm leaving meetings abruptly and making the rest of the team have to work around me. And it's affecting things at home, too. My husband... he says it feels like I'm barely even present anymore.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

Yeah, I have. I used to be really active... I'd actually plan my whole week around going to salsa dancing, my book club, yoga classes, or even just having friends over to cook Guatemalan food. But lately... I just don't have the energy or the desire for any of it. I mostly just cancel my plans now and sit at home. I end up just scrolling on my phone or pretending to watch a TV show, but I'm not really paying attention.
Do you often think that you're a bad person or that you're worthless because of what happened during the cutover incident?
No, not really. I mean, I don't think I'm a bad person or worthless. I just... I feel terrible about how it all went down and the impact it had, but I don't think it makes me a bad person overall.
Are there any activities that you used to find very meaningful or enjoyable that you've lost interest in since the cutover incident?

Well, like I mentioned just a minute ago... yeah. It's mostly the things I brought up earlier. My salsa dancing, the book club, yoga classes, and having people over to cook. I used to find all of that really meaningful, but... I just don't have the drive for any of it anymore.
Are there any other activities besides the ones you mentioned, such as hobbies or spending time with friends and family, that you've lost interest in since the cutover incident?

No, not really. It's pretty much just the things I already mentioned. I mean, I guess spending time with friends is wrapped up in all of that, since I don't really see them for book club or dinner anymore, but there aren't any other specific hobbies or anything else I've dropped. It's just... those main things I used to do.
Are there any other activities that you used to enjoy, besides the ones you mentioned, that you've lost interest in since the cutover incident?
Um, no. Like I just said, there really isn't anything else. I can't think of any other hobbies or things I used to enjoy that I've dropped. It's really just the ones we just went over.
Are there any other activities besides the ones you mentioned that you used to find very enjoyable, but now you don't?
I feel like we're going in circles a bit here... but no, there's really nothing else. Just the things I've already listed for you. I don't have any other hobbies or activities to add to that list.
Do you have trouble trusting yourself or your own judgment since the cutover incident?

No, not really. I mean, I still trust my own judgment just fine. The incident was bad, but it didn't make me doubt my own decisions or anything. I still feel confident in my choices, especially at work, so... no, I wouldn't say I have trouble trusting myself.
